conventions.convention: Empirical squared loss is ||y−Xβ||²/(2n). Lasso adds λ||β||₁, so the equivalent published convention is n⁻¹||y−Xβ||²+2λ||β||₁.
Ridge uses the unaveraged objective ||y−Xβ||²+λ||β||² with λ>0. An explicitly separate intercept uses the stated unpenalized-intercept convention.
Orthonormal design means XᵀX=I_p, rather than nI_p. The Lasso threshold is nλ; sign(0)=0 and (u)₊=max(u,0).

Signed-support success means existence of an optimizer with sign(β̂)=sign(β*), including zeros off the true support. The Gaussian models have independent observations, independent design and noise, unit-diagonal covariance, and no separate intercept.
The matrix infinity norm is the maximum absolute row sum. Conditional covariance is the displayed Schur complement; the corresponding block of the inverse covariance is its inverse.
The Gaussian helper lemmas explicitly assume AC. The upper-threshold refutation additionally states DC and countable choice to match its published Gaussian Lipschitz concentration supplier.

load_bearing.statement: Assume AC. Let d_k,n_k≥1 be integer sequences with d_k/n_k→0. For each k, let G_k∈R^{n_k×d_k} have mutually independent N(0,1) entries. Then ||G_kᵀG_k/n_k−I_{d_k}||op→0 in probability.

Assume AC. Let r_k,n_k be positive integers with n_k→∞ and r_k/n_k→1. For each k, let Z_{k,1},…,Z_{k,r_k} be independent N(0,1) random variables and set D_k=Σ_j Z_{k,j}². Then D_k/n_k→1 in probability.
Assume AC. Let m≥2, and let X,Y∈R^m be independent, centered Gaussian vectors with finite covariance matrices. If E[(X_i−X_j)²]≥E[(Y_i−Y_j)²] for every i,j∈{1,…,m}, then E[max_i X_i]≥E[max_i Y_i].
Assume AC. There is an integer m₀ such that for every m≥m₀ and independent standard-normal random variables G₁,…,G_m, E[max_{1≤i≤m}G_i]≥(1/4)√log m.

Let X∈R^{n×p}, y∈R^n, λ>0, and nonempty S⊆{1,…,p}. Assume X_S has full column rank. If an optimizer of ||y−Xβ||²/(2n)+λ||β||₁ has support exactly S and active sign vector b, then β̂_S=(X_SᵀX_S/n)⁻¹(X_Sᵀy/n−λb). This is a necessary active-coordinate condition only.
Let n,p≥1, X∈R^{n×p} satisfy XᵀX=I_p, y∈R^n, and λ>0. The objective ||y−Xβ||²/(2n)+λ||β||₁ has the unique minimizer β̂_j=S_{nλ}((Xᵀy)_j), where S_a(t)=sign(t)(|t|−a)₊.

For n,p≥1, X∈R^{n×p}, and y∈R^n, OLS minimizers are exactly the solutions of XᵀXβ=Xᵀy and form β₀+ker X. This set is a singleton iff the columns of X are linearly independent. For every λ>0, ||y−Xβ||²+λ||β||² has unique minimizer (XᵀX+λI_p)⁻¹Xᵀy.
